file.content:
# evalmerge

A pipeline that ingests model-evaluation results from three heterogeneous
harness formats, normalizes them to a canonical schema, deduplicates,
validates, loads everything into SQLite, and emits a data-quality report.

Requires Python 3.11+ and uses only the standard library (`csv`, `json`,
`xml.etree`, `sqlite3`). Tests use `pytest`.

## Usage

The CLI can be run directly as a module:

```sh
python -m evalmerge ingest <dir> [--db evalmerge.db]
python -m evalmerge report [--db evalmerge.db]
```

or installed as a console script:

```sh
pip install -e .
evalmerge ingest data/
evalmerge report
```

`ingest` discovers input files by directory layout under `<dir>`:

| Source | Location | Format |
| ------ | -------- | ------ |
| `a` | `harness_a/*.csv` | CSV: `run_id,model,task,score,timestamp,meta` |
| `b` | `harness_b/*.jsonl` | JSON lines with `id`, `model_name`, `benchmark`, `metrics`, `ts`, `tags` |
| `c` | `harness_c/results.xml` | `<results><run id="...">...</run></results>` |

### Generating sample data

`generate_fixtures.py` deterministically (seeded) writes a fixture tree that
exercises every supported input quirk at least twice:

```sh
python generate_fixtures.py data/
python -m evalmerge ingest data/
python -m evalmerge report
```

## Canonical schema

All rows land in the SQLite table `results`:

| Column | Type | Notes |
| ------ | ---- | ----- |
| `run_id` | TEXT | harness-assigned run identifier |
| `source` | TEXT | `a`, `b`, or `c`; `UNIQUE(run_id, source)` |
| `model` | TEXT | normalized: lowercase, whitespace/underscores collapsed to hyphens |
| `task` | TEXT | benchmark/task name |
| `score` | REAL | always in `[0, 1]` |
| `stderr` | REAL | nullable; only Format B provides it |
| `ts_utc` | TEXT | RFC3339, always UTC (`...Z`) |
| `raw_extra` | TEXT | JSON: Format A meta, Format B tags, Format C unit attribute |

Auxiliary tables: `warnings` (structured validation warnings from the latest
ingest pass), `model_aliases` (every raw model spelling seen per normalized
name), and `ingest_stats` (e.g. duplicate corrections applied).

## Input handling and validation rules

Format quirks handled transparently: UTF-8 BOMs and rows over-split by
unquoted comma-bearing `meta` (Format A); blank lines, literal `null` lines,
millisecond epochs, and inconsistent model spellings (Format B); date-only
timestamps treated as midnight UTC (Format C). For Format B, duplicate `id`s
are corrections: within an ingest pass files are processed in sorted name
order and the later occurrence wins.

Each validation rule produces a structured warning record rather than a
crash:

| Rule | Condition | Action |
| ---- | --------- | ------ |
| `score_out_of_range` | score outside `[0, 1]` after normalization | clamp, keep row |
| `unparseable_timestamp` | timestamp/date/epoch cannot be parsed | skip row |
| `invalid_meta_json` | Format A `meta` is not valid JSON | keep row, store meta as a JSON string |
| `missing_score` | score absent or non-numeric | skip row |
| `unknown_unit` | Format C `unit` not `percent`/`fraction` | assume percent if value > 1 else fraction, keep row |
| `malformed_row` | row/line structurally unusable | skip row |

`report` prints rows ingested per source, rows skipped per rule, non-fatal
warning counts, duplicate corrections applied, a min/median/max score summary
per model, and every model observed under two or more unnormalized spellings.

Ingest is deterministic and idempotent: re-running on the same inputs leaves
the database logically identical (asserted in the tests via a sorted row dump
of every table, since SQLite's internal page layout is not byte-stable).

## Testing

```sh
pytest
```

The suite generates fixtures into a temporary directory and asserts that
every planted quirk is handled as specified, that re-ingestion is idempotent,
that later-file corrections win, and that the report's skip counts exactly
match the planted defects.
